topicName: Playbook Syntax, Structure, and Execution Flow
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Playbook Syntax, Structure, and Execution Flow in Ansible"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ansible playbooks are the core of configuration management and deployment automation. Written in YAML, they describe the desired state of your systems, making complex multi-tier deployments repeatable and easy to understand."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. YAML Syntax Rules in Ansible"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Indentation is crucial. Always use spaces for indentation, never tabs. Two spaces per indentation level is the standard convention."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Lists are represented by a dash (-) followed by a space."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Key-value pairs are represented using a colon followed by a space (key: value)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Basic Playbook Structure"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"A playbook consists of one or more plays. Each play maps a group of hosts to a set of tasks. Below is a standard playbook structure."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"---
- name: Configure Web Server
  hosts: webservers
  become: yes
  vars:
    http_port: 80
  tasks:
    - name: Ensure Apache is installed
      apt:
        name: apache2
        state: present

    - name: Start Apache service
      service:
        name: apache2
        state: started
        enabled: yes"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Execution Flow"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ansible executes playbooks from top to bottom, strictly in the order tasks are written. Understanding the execution flow involves several key phases:"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gathering Facts: By default, Ansible runs the setup module to gather system facts about the target hosts before executing tasks."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Task Iteration: Tasks are executed sequentially across all targeted hosts. A host must successfully complete a task before moving to the next one in the play."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Handlers: Handlers are special tasks that only run when notified by another task and when that task reports a 'changed' state. Handlers are executed at the very end of the play."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Example Using Handlers"},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"---
- name: Deploy Configuration
  hosts: all
  tasks:
    - name: Copy configuration file
      template:
        src: templates/nginx.conf.j2
        dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
      notify: Restart Nginx

  handlers:
    - name: Restart Nginx
      service:
        name: nginx
        state: restarted"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering playbook syntax, correct indentation, and the sequential execution flow enables you to build robust, idempotent, and scalable automation workflows in Ansible."}]
